title: Dynamical signatures of deconfined spinons in dimerized sawtooth chains
authors: Nishan Ranabhat, Brandon B. Le, Seung-Hun Lee, Gia-Wei Chern
abstract: We study the ground-state properties and dynamical response of the Heisenberg model on the sawtooth chain in and away from the exactly solvable valence-bond-solid (VBS) point. We employ U(1)-symmetric density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and time-dependent variational principle (TDVP) methods to compute equilibrium diagnostics and the zero-temperature dynamical structure factor (DSF) $S^{zz}(q,ω)$ across the dimerized phase, a valence-bond-ordered state in which the two symmetry-equivalent apex--base bonds of each triangle develop unequal spin correlations, probing the approach to the continuous lower phase boundary, the exact VBS point, and the approach to the first-order upper boundary. In every regime, the DSF is a broad continuum dominated by a bright band at its lower edge, with the intensity at the one-triplon energy $ω\simeq J_{AB}$ suppressed. We identify the spectrum as a deconfined two-spinon continuum of kink and antikink domain walls between the two degenerate singlet coverings. Closed-form spinon dispersions fix the continuum edges and track the dominant band across the zone in all three regimes, while an explicit finite-separation two-kink calculation in a constrained Hilbert space reproduces the measured intensity distribution. Our results provide a microscopic picture of fractionalized excitations in the dimerized sawtooth chain and are relevant to the recently discovered Ti$^{3+}$ kagome fluorides, where strongly anisotropic exchange interactions can generate sawtooth-chain building blocks.
summary: This work analyzes the quantum spin dynamics of the sawtooth chain, a model for frustrated quantum magnets. Using DMRG and TDVP, the authors show that the low-energy excitations are not simple quasiparticles but rather a broad continuum of deconfined two-spinons. This provides a key theoretical insight into fractionalization relevant to materials like kagome fluorides.
main_problem: The study investigates the ground-state properties and dynamical response of the Heisenberg model on the sawtooth chain, focusing on the nature of fractionalized excitations (spinons) in the dimerized phase.
main_result: The dynamical structure factor is found to be dominated by a broad two-spinon continuum, rather than a simple one-triplon mode, providing a microscopic picture of fractionalized excitations.
method: The research employs advanced numerical techniques including U(1)-symmetric DMRG for ground states and TDVP for dynamics, complemented by analytical derivations of two-kink models.
model_or_system: The system is the antiferromagnetic sawtooth chain, modeled by a Heisenberg Hamiltonian involving interactions between basal and apical spins. The analysis explores different regimes controlled by the ratio of exchange couplings, $r = J_{BB}/J_{AB}$.
key_observables: Zero-temperature dynamical structure factor ($S^{zz}(q, \omega)$), dimer order ($C_{	ext{dimer}}$), and bipartite entanglement entropy ($S(b)$).
important_parameters: The ratio $r = J_{BB}/J_{AB}$ controls the phase, with specific focus on the VBS point ($r=1$) and transitions to gapless phases.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the continuum to a two-kink model and uses approximations like the linear ramp approximation for closed-form derivations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dual signatures of energy and entanglement entropy across different coupling regimes ($r=0.72, 1.00, 1.38$), confirming phase transitions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system across different coupling regimes using DMRG and TDVP to calculate static and dynamic observables, culminating in a detailed two-kink construction to map out the spinon continuum.
why_interesting: The identification of a deconfined two-spinon continuum provides a concrete theoretical model for understanding fractionalization in geometrically frustrated quantum magnets, which is highly relevant to strongly correlated materials.
